questions.question: Were the successful earlier book pages directly supplied to the image generator?
questions.answer: No. Every persisted PR6 request has reference_image_paths equal to an empty array.

questions.question: If so, which exact images?
questions.answer: None. No benchmark PDF page, character image or location image was supplied as a generation input.
evidence: reference_image_paths=[] in all eight request records

questions.question: If not, why not?
questions.answer: The active character-reference registry contained no HUMAN_APPROVED_EXACT_ASSET binding and reported TEXT_ONLY_PENDING_STYLE_APPROVAL. PR6 did not yet contain a curated page-reference manifest or role-aware reference package.

questions.question: Was the prompt primarily asking for a standalone illustration rather than a comic panel?
questions.answer: Yes. Each request described a portrait 3:4 internal illustration proof as one generated raster. The prompt used the page-level narrative_beats field and proof composition, not a selected panel geometry and reading-order package. Only the full-page proof was naturally aligned with that unit.
evidence: Asset type: Khatakshetra DM04 internal illustration proof; artwork only, no lettering

questions.question: Did the model receive conflicting instructions?
questions.answer: The requests contained a material ambiguity: Devī's text registry calls for a many-armed identity, while the common avoid list includes extra limb. Battle page 17 also combines the counter-arrow exchange and its later equipment-loss consequence into one full-canvas request. These are demonstrable prompt tensions, but their exact effect on the unsurfaced model cannot be proven.
evidence: prompt contains many-armed identity and Avoid: extra limb

questions.question: Did reference-conditioning actually execute?
questions.answer: No. All requests used operation=generate and empty reference_image_paths. The receipts bind generated output but record no submitted visual reference.

questions.question: Is the underlying model identity known?
questions.answer: No. Provider metadata records model=NOT_SURFACED_BY_BUILTIN_TOOL. It is unsupported to infer model quality or identity from the pixels.

questions.question: Does the tool support image editing or reference-guided generation?
questions.answer: PR6 capability metadata declares generate, edit and reference_conditioning for the Codex built-in image tool. However, durable provider-side evidence that reference conditioning works in a future session has not yet been captured.
questions.qualification: Capability declared; PR6 execution path for edit/reference input untested.

questions.question: Did later prompts lose the earlier books' visual identity?
questions.answer: The earlier page pixels were never in the PR6 context. Both attempt rounds repeated a textual style summary, so the generator could approximate navy/gold ornament and painterly finish but could not align to the benchmarks' actual page rhythm, expressions or lettering hierarchy.
evidence: identical textual Style/medium line in persisted prompts

questions.question: Was visual QA comparing images against real reference pages?
questions.answer: No. PR6 review assessed series_identity as a semantic dimension, but the review requests contain no exact Gold Standard page IDs, paths or hashes and no side-by-side evidence artifact.

additional_findings.finding: All eight outputs are genuine readable 1086x1448 PNGs. No post-generation crop or resize changed their composition; receipts record IDENTITY_COPY normalization.

Page-level prompts with many subjects, weapons and temporal clauses encourage emblematic poster composition instead of sequential storytelling. This is strongest in the divine, battle and decisive-victory requests.

A uniform top safe-region instruction was applied even to immersive pages without first designing the exact page lettering. This encouraged empty-sky poster layouts and still did not reliably preserve the specified geometry.
The prompt builder resolved the entire selected character records into long text sections and a union of exclusions, but did not attach exact role-labeled visual references or panel geometry.
Provider-side sampling parameters, seed, internal image model revision, safety transformations and detailed reference-conditioning behavior were not surfaced.
The repository cannot independently invoke the session-scoped Codex image tool or prove future availability. A host-injected execution boundary is still required.
Deterministic repository code cannot judge emotional expressiveness, complex religious iconography or cultural authenticity from pixels. Those judgments require an image-capable independent reviewer.

largest_quality_gap: PR6 optimized a single ornate painting per proof. The benchmark books derive their storybook quality from page design: changing shot scale, explicit reaction beats, panel-to-panel causality, character emotion, environmental continuity and exact lettering hierarchy.
non_conclusion: There is no evidence that Codex used an inferior image model. The verified gap is in reference delivery, production-unit choice, prompt construction and comparative QA; model identity remains unknown.
